result_text:
Folders whose names start with `mock` or `__mock` are now classed as mock-resources test code, whatever follows the prefix, including plain `mock/`, punctuation, and non-ASCII names.

**Change:** `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (the `addTestConventions` method). The two folder patterns were `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`. They now read `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`. The `[^/\\]*` part matches any run of characters within one folder name, so it cannot cross a separator. The existing `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mockStore/` and similar folders still match, since they are a subset of the new pattern. `mockapi/`, `Mocks/` and `_mock.*` files are untouched.

**Test:** new `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockTest.java`. It covers the three new folder kinds, backslash paths, the previously matched names, and the negative cases (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

**Verification:** the new test class passes (3 tests), `SourceFileFilterTest` passes, and the full `codeanalyzer` module passes offline (333 run, 0 failures, 3 skipped that were already skipped). I did not commit.

One thing I kept as it was: the `.*/` prefix still requires a parent path segment, so a `mock/` folder at the very root of a relative path with no leading directory would not match. That was already true before this change.
